messages:
emily (customer): Hey team — hitting a weird streaming issue in prod. Client reconnects mid-response and we get a partial JSON chunk, then a duplicate partial when it reconnects. Customer is seeing doubled billing for the same prompt.

maria (support): Thanks for reporting — can you paste the request pattern? Are you using token rotation or ephemeral session tokens?

emily (customer): Using our normal session token that's rotated every 30m. Sequence: start SSE -> partial JSON (truncated) -> client detects disconnect -> client reconnects with same session token -> server resumes but sends second partial overlapping the first. Billing shows two "generation" charges for one logical response.

maria (support): Oof. Do you have a minimal repro or logs? Any request IDs?

emily (customer): I grabbed wire logs and server request-id headers. Example (redacted):
```
GET /v1/streams?model=gpt-open&session=eyJ...token
accept: text/event-stream
x-request-id: 01FXYZ-abc
```
Server stream: first event ends with `..."choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, wor"` then disconnect. On reconnect with same session token we get `delta":{"content":"ld"}` prefixed again by server which leads our client to assemble `Hello, worldld`.

raj (eng): That sounds like a resume / epoch mismatch. On reconnect we should either resume from KV cache offset or start a new stream; duplicates sound like we were re-sending unacknowledged tokens. Can you share the reconnect headers?

emily (customer): Reconnect headers include `x-resume-offset: 0` (we're just passing the session id), and `x-client-epoch: 1` from our client. The first connection had epoch 0.

maria (support): @raj any known regressions around epoch handling? We had a middleware change last week touching resumption windows.

raj (eng): I pulled logs for that request-id. Server accepted reconnect and matched session token but didn't validate `x-client-epoch` properly — so it replayed the tail of the in-flight buffer instead of trimming already-sent fragments. Could explain duplicate partials and double billing because both fragments were counted. Looks like a regression in `resume_manager` introduced in commit 1a2b3c.

linda (prod): We have metrics showing a spike in "stream_resume" events with overlapping offsets on 2026-02-20 18:00 UTC. Rolling back the 1a2b3c patch reduced overlap but didn't fully revert behavior on long-running sessions.

maria (support): Immediate mitigation for the customer?

raj (eng): Quick fixes: 1) Server-side: refuse resume when `x-client-epoch` < server epoch, returning a clean `event: session_reset` so client restarts and no duplicate token accounting. 2) Client-side: on reconnect, include `x-last-acked-offset` and dedupe deltas before applying.

emily (customer): Can you do server-side check for us? We can't push a client change quickly. This customer has billing impact.

raj (eng): I'll patch resume_manager to validate epoch + last-ack and return `400` with `event: resume_reject` for mismatched epochs. That will force clients to start fresh. Pushing a hotfix to canary now.

deploy-bot: roll triggered by raj — patch/resume-epoch-validation -> canary (env=prod-canary-1) — started

linda (prod): Can we also emit a metric and link the request-id so support can reconcile billing? Add `x-resume-action: reject-epoch` header and a short log line.

raj (eng): Done — added header and a trace id in logs. Canary up: 1718032690. I'm watching customer request-id.

emily (customer): Re-tested — client retried and got a resume_reject, then did a fresh full request and got one clean response. Billing showed single charge. Thanks.

maria (support): Filing internal postmortem and billing cleanup request. Emily, we'll reconcile the duplicate charge if it shows up on your invoice — please DM invoice id. Sorry for the hit. :hugging_face:

emily (customer): DM sent. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

raj (eng): Follow-ups: add unit tests for epoch validation, add integration test that simulates partial frames + reconnect with stale epoch, and a migration to make resume strict-by-default in the next release. I'll create GH PR and link here.

maria (support): Tagging this as P1 for billing-impacting streaming regressions. Closing thread after billing handled and PR merged. :white_check_mark:
